overview:
### Release workflow: stage npm publishes for maintainer approval. Difficulty: 3/5

This change stops the release workflow from publishing straight to npm. Instead, the version goes into npm's stage queue, and a maintainer has to approve it on npmjs.com with 2FA before it goes live. A stolen or misused CI run can therefore no longer ship a package to users by itself. In the release job, the workflow first upgrades the runner's npm to `^11.15.0`, the first version with `npm stage`. It then swaps `npm publish` for `npm stage publish --access public --provenance`, still authenticating through OIDC trusted publishing. The header comment now describes the stage-only trusted publisher.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Tag push v*"] --> B["setup-node 24, registry npmjs.org"]
    B --> C["npm install -g npm@^11.15.0"]
    C --> D["npm stage publish --access public --provenance (OIDC)"]
    D --> E{"Stage accepted?"}
    E -->|"no"| F["Job fails"]
    E -->|"yes"| G["Create GitHub Release (gh)"]
    D -.->|"queued"| H{"Maintainer approves on npmjs.com (2FA)?"}
    H -->|"yes"| I["Version live on npm"]
    H -->|"no"| J["Version never published"]
    class C,D,H chg
    classDef chg fill:#d6ffd9,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#111
```

**Riskiest area:** the GitHub Release is now created as soon as staging succeeds, before anyone approves it. A release can exist for a version that never reaches npm. Also, the npm upgrade uses a floating caret range on a supply-chain-sensitive publish step.

comments.body:
Pin `npm` to an exact version instead of the `^11.15.0` caret range. The caret resolves to the latest npm 11.x at run time, making the release pipeline non-deterministic; any future npm 11.x patch can silently change `npm stage publish` behavior in a production release job.
